{{Short description|Italian mathematician and engineer}}
{{Orphan|date=July 2026}}

[[File:Gargiolli, Gugliemo - Iride celeste, 1655 - BEIC 879943.jpg|thumb|''Iride celeste'', title page (1655)]]

'''Guglielmo Gargiolli''' was a [[17th-century]] [[Italians|Italian]] [[mathematician]] and [[engineer]].<ref>{{Cite book|first=Giovanni|last=Targioni-Tozzetti|author-link=Giovanni Targioni Tozzetti|title=Ragionamento sopra le cause, e sopra i rimedj dell'insalubrità d'aria della Valdinievole|volume=1|publisher=Stamperia Imperiale|date=1761|pp=150–154|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Kxec8mvOKL0C&pg=PA150|language=it}}</ref>

He was Lecturer of Mathematics at the [[University of Siena]], and Lecturer of [[Military engineering|Military Engineering]] and Mathematics at the Court of [[Florence]]. His book, ''Iride celeste'' ("Celestial Iris"), was noted for its explanation of how to estimate from a [[distance]] the [[height]] of an object and its distance from the observer.<ref>{{Cite book|first=Giovanni|last=Targioni-Tozzetti|author-link=Giovanni Targioni Tozzetti|title=Atti e memorie inedite dell'Accademia del Cimento, e notizie aneddote dei progressi delle scienze in Toscana|volume=1|publisher=Giuseppe Tofani|date=1780|p=334|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_wFlAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA334|language=it}}</ref>
